page: Microsoft Azure M416-208s_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MSv2 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 208 dedicated vCPUs derived from 104 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280L processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 5700.0 GB of system memory, providing 27.4 GB of RAM per core. It includes 8389 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, but does not feature any GPU coprocessors.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the bottom 25% tier. Conversely, multi-core capabilities are highly competitive, with stress-ng multi-core performance, PassMark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranking in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read operations placing in the top 10% tier.

Given its massive memory footprint of 5.7 TB and high resource density, this server represents a specialized hardware class where cost efficiency is realized through consolidating massive in-memory workloads rather than raw single-threaded compute. The server is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, such as SAP HANA or Redis, where it achieved a top-tier 162.62 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. It is also appropriate for heavy multi-threaded data processing, software compilation, and enterprise database operations.
description: Microsoft Azure M416-208s_v2 is a memory-optimized server in the MSv2 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8280L processor with 208 vCPUs (104 physical cores) running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 5700.0 GB of RAM, 8389 GB of local storage, and is Premium Storage capable without GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks show a significant tradeoff: single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression are weak, ranking in the bottom 25%, whereas multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and memory bandwidth are in the top 10% tier. This resource density makes the server highly efficient for consolidating massive in-memory databases and enterprise workloads. It is best suited for large-scale database operations, Redis deployments, and heavy multi-threaded data processing tasks.
